series: Things Living In Your House, Part 11
sources: Utah State University Extension, Booklice fact sheet (Utah Pests): booklice are flat, pale, soft-bodied, 1-4 mm long; do not feed on bindings or glue but on mold and other fungi present in books; also occur in rugs, stored grains, damp construction materials; many but not all species reproduce parthenogenetically, all females that do not require fertilization by males; life cycle 4 weeks to 2 months, a single generation in as few as 25 days under ideal conditions; do not bite or transmit disease; control by decreasing humidity and increasing airflow; https://extension.usu.edu/pests/uppdl/files/factsheet/booklice.pdf

Utah State University Extension IPM, Booklice and Psocids: indoors found in damp books, around leaking or sweating pipes, in voids and cardboard boxes; eat mold spores; indicator of moisture issues; https://extension.usu.edu/planthealth/ipm/notes_nuisance/booklice-psocids

Clemson Cooperative Extension HGIC, Booklice: not true lice, related to barklice; do not bite people or pets; feed on mold, and starchy foods like flour, grains and dried fruit; damage damp books by feeding on moldy paper; ideal 75-90% relative humidity; 50-60% is harmful and they can die within weeks if humidity stays low; keep humidity below 50%; large populations build up in newly built structures because fresh plaster and drywall hold moisture that supports mold; https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/booklice/

title: Many Bugs in Your Old Books Are All Female, No Males Needed 📚
tiktok_caption: the tiny bugs in your old books aren't eating the pages 📚 they're eating mold you can't see, and many kinds don't need males. Would you still read a book that had them? 📖 yes / 🗑️ toss it

beats.say: Many of the tiny bugs in your old books are all female. No males needed.
Booklice. Pale, soft, and about a millimeter long.
And they're not real lice. They don't bite you.
They aren't eating your books. They're eating the mold growing on them.
Mold so thin you usually can't even see it.
So if you've got booklice, you've got damp.
Subscribe. Part twelve has pincers, and it hides in your bathroom.
